newsitem.title: SPAIN: Iberia counts cost of Madrid airport closure.
newsitem.headline: Iberia counts cost of Madrid airport closure.

text.p: Tuesday night's five hour closure of Madrid's Barajas airport cost flag carrier Iberia more than 65 million pesetas, the airline said in a statement.
Iberia cancelled 95 flights, diverted 11 more to alternative airports and said a further 55 suffered delays of around two hours. Other airlines were affected to a lesser extent.
The shutdown, caused by an electricity failure following a fire in an underground gallery, was the first in the airport's history and forced the cancellation of 300 flights in total.

Iberia alone said 15,000 of its passengers were affected and it had to accomodate nearly 1,000 of them in hotels in various Spanish cities and transport a further 1,200 by bus to Madrid from provincial capitals.
It used another 14 buses to take passengers to hotels or railway stations within Madrid.
On top of this 14 domestic and European flights were cancelled on Wednesday morning because aircraft or crew were in the wrong places.
Airlines have been complaining about growing delays at Barajas, which is working at or above full capacity, for the last two months.
The airports authority AENA said on Wednesday that it was reviewing all safety procedures to ensure the closure would never be repeated.

AENA is also preparing the former U.S. air base at nearby Torrejon to handle some flights to relieve congestion at Barajas, possibly starting next week. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44-171-542-7706 Fax+44-171-542-5017
